turns.content:
Julian called my index funds "training wheels" in front of people I barely know.

I told him I'm not coming to his mixer and not investing. Pretty blunt. Maybe too blunt?

He's my friend since college. I don't want drama. I just want him to drop it without me having to block him or send an ultimatum. Was that reasonable?

Yes—based on what you described, that was reasonable. Calling your index funds “training wheels” in front of near-strangers was a put-down, even if he meant it as teasing. You’re allowed to decline both the mixer and the investment without defending your choices.

**Blunt isn’t necessarily unkind.** “I’m not coming, and I’m not investing” is clear. Unless you added personal insults, there’s nothing here that obviously needs an apology.

Since you want to keep the friendship, you can soften the tone without changing the answer—*if* another message feels necessary:

> “Hey, I was direct because the training-wheels comment didn’t sit well with me. I’m happy with my investments, and I’m passing on the mixer. I’d rather keep investing out of our friendship. Still up for catching up another time.”

That’s a boundary, not an ultimatum: no threat, no demand that he agree. If he pitches again, keep it short: “No thanks, I’m all set,” then change the subject. You don’t need to build a better argument for a decision that’s already yours to make.

And if he’s already dropped it, you can let it rest. A clear no doesn’t require a cleanup operation.

that draft you wrote… i like it. gentle but clear.

think i'll use that if he nudges again. thanks.

one thing though—i don't want to cut him off. i know people say protect your peace, block, move on. but i'd rather handle it quiet. that's my call.

It is your call. Wanting to keep an old friendship while saying no to an investment isn’t a contradiction—and you don’t have to cut him off to make your no count.

Letting it rest unless he nudges again sounds consistent with what you want. You can be warm toward Julian without reopening the pitch. No big confrontation required.

he just texted.

“bigger picture, man. don't let fear keep you small.”

i was gonna send your draft. now i'm annoyed again. still want to keep it soft though.

That would be irritating—he’s treating your decision as fear rather than taking your no seriously. You can keep it soft without defending yourself:

> “Hey man, I know you’re excited about this, but I’m happy with my approach and I’m going to pass on the investment and mixer. Let’s leave investing out of it. Would still be good to catch up another time.”

You don’t need to prove you’re brave enough to invest. Just keep the decision closed and the friendship open.

sent your draft. he replied "fair enough, door's open."

so it worked. no drama. friendship still there.

guess i just needed to hear it was okay to say no quiet.

Yep. A quiet no is still a complete no—you didn’t have to get harsher to make it count.

You were clear, he accepted it, and the friendship has room to carry on. “Door’s open” doesn’t require another reply or any future commitment. You can leave it right there.

yeah. you get it.

that's all i needed. just a quiet no.

thanks.
You’re welcome. A quiet no, and back to being friends.
